questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university of Milan offers a lot of different course for law students, which i thought sounded interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The overall experience of exchange was good. It is fun to live in a different country with a different culture, and so is going to a different school with a quite different way of structuring the teachings. It was fun interacting with the other exchange students and there was plenty of arrangements made for exchange students, which made that seamless to do.
I did however have many difficulties with my landlord, which was a thorn in the side. And i also found it a bit disappointing, that i had very limited interactions with Italiens in the same age range as me, this was among other things because the classes in english were almost only attended by exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. All the information was made available primarily through mails that was sent out at the appropriate times. Furthermore the erasmus office at the school are very friendly and helpful, so if you ever have any questions, they will happily help you out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Upon arrival you go to the erasmus office, where i got my student card and my proof of attendance signed for the first time. Here you also got various information and answers to any questions you had.
There is also a student organization called ESN, which had a welcome meeting, where they gave a lot of helpful information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: At first glance there are many options. However when you have to find housing through AirBnB or websites like it, the landlord can often cancel whenever without any real reasoning for it. This happened to me many times and made it quite difficult to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The websites where you can find housing is often only a service for connection landlords and tenants, meaning that they do not really help if any problems occur. So make an extensive and unambiguous agreement with the landlord themselves, and write it all down in a contract.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration itself is easy. However, a lot of the courses have their classes at the same time, which is a problem as attendance is mandatory. This makes it a big puzzle to find and pick courses for 30 ECTS point which do not overlap.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a big catalogue of courses from where you can choose which ones you want. In the specific course in the catalogue there is a link to a calendar, where you can see when the classes are. When you have picked some courses, then you go to the student portal (Unimia), where you just write which courses you picked.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The process was described in an email. Besides that i am not sure, as i did not use any other help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As far as i know you can pick any class, without any rejection or the like. I do not think they make a cap on how many students can attend the different courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To make sure you find different courses that do not overlap, as the attendance is mandatory. And as the courses can be at different campus', also check which campus the courses are in, as you might not have time to go from one campus to another, if you pick to classes which are right after each other.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level to be lower in Milan than it is in Copenhagen. However, there is also something to be said about how the teaching is structured differently. In Copenhagen classes are not mandatory and you are not evaluated on in class performances, however there is a difficult (mostly written) exam at the end. In Milan the classes are mandatory and you are evaluated on in class performance, however, the exams at the end are easier and often oral.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching in Milan is mostly just the teacher presenting the material and asking questions to the students. In Copenhagen you have to prepare presentations and cases for the classes, which i barely had any of on exchange.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. INTERNATIONAL REFUGEE PROTECTION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
2. TRADE LIBERALIZATION AND LABOUR RIGHTS
3. EUROPEAN MONETARY AND ECONOMIC LAW
4. COMPETITION LAW AND ECONOMICS
5. LAW AND POLICIES FOR SOCIAL RIGHTS PROTECTION IN EUROPE

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
COMPETITION LAW AND ECONOMICS is a very well made course with a good teacher, but it was also the hardest course i had on exchange.
EUROPEAN MONETARY AND ECONOMIC LAW is a very interesting course if you are into european law. 
LAW AND POLICIES FOR SOCIAL RIGHTS PROTECTION IN EUROPE also has a good teacher and is a not only instructive but also thought-provoking course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Lawyer fees for the problems with my landlord.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation is way cheaper than i expected.
Housing is more expensive than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I did not attend any, and i do not really know if there was any.
But there was the student organization "ESN", which made many arrangements.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know if the university actually provided any, besides an italian course.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sightseeing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The horse racing course next to the san siro, and of course going to see football matches at the san siro. Also taking the trains to different italian cities, it is easy and fast to get there, and it is fun to experience different cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It probably takes a week or two, but it is not difficult in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. As i mentioned above there are almost only exchange students in the english courses, and as there are not many activities arranged by the university, then you probably have to seek them out elsewhere.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of Italians do not speak english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How laid back and unworried it is. It also seems that most problems can be fixed if you ask nice enough.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Check when the classes are for the different courses, so you do not get overlapping classes.
2. Make a contract with your landlord.
3. Show up to the arrangements made by the student organizations (especially at the start of your exchange).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to find your classroom at first, so go to the campus before you actually start school, and find out where the different classrooms are.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all parts of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My rental situation with my landlord.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
